ECD 123.description: This course aims to develop the language skills of the child and the development of language fluency that enables them to express himself and his ideas fluently, and depends on the mechanisms of building linguistic concepts in the child, whether Arabic or English, and how to master, and the use of diverse techniques to develop the ability to express self and communicate with others and learn Diverse cultures through mastering language skills.

ECD 126.title: Arabic Language in Kindergarten
ECD 126.description: The course is concerned with the basics of teaching Arabic to the child in kindergarten stage, and the importance of preserving the cultural identity of the child. And the development of his native language through teaching and learning strategies. The course also focuses on the concept of language and speech and the development of child linguistic abilities with a focus on increasing his language skills and his ability to express himself as well as the development of creativity and storytelling.

ECD 127.title: Foreign Language in Kindergarten
ECD 127.description: This course aims to teach the child foreign languages as skills to communicate with other communities, and develop his ability to read in a language other than his mother tongue (English), and work to develop the capabilities of expressive language fluency through writing and storytelling in foreign language, and the ability to communicate with foreigners in their own language while maintaining On the national language.

ECD 128.title: Psychology of Play
ECD 128.description: This course focuses on the importance of play for kindergarten children, and the role of the teacher in the use of educational approaches to achieve the targeted learning outcomes through play, and the practice of diverse activities, as well as the skills acquired by the child through play, merit performance, treatment therapy, and the development of creative imagination. It also help the child to acquire diverse experiences and the impact of play on the child's normal personality and his contribution to the integration of psychological construction.

ECD 129.title: Child Culture and Information
ECD 129.description: This course focuses on the formation of media culture in kindergarten children using strategies to build media awareness. This will be done through expanding its cognitive awareness and linking education with the surrounding environment, developing his ability to educate himself, and qualifying the kindergarten teacher to help the child to form his own media through the establishment of a daily newspaper or a magazine that includes his activities and daily practices, in addition to the preparation of a children's newsletter.

ECF343.title: Pediatric Diseases
ECF343.description: Health, disease - pathogens - ways of spreading infectious diseases, and their complications - ways of caring for a sick child - infectious diseases (1) diseases transmitted; by droplets (measles - mumps - chickenpox) - (2) diseases transmitted; by contaminated food and drink (intestinal flu) - (3) diseases transmitted; by blood (malaria) - (4) diseases transmitted; by contact (scabies - lice) - non-infectious diseases: non-infectious respiratory diseases (chest allergy) - endocrine diseases (diabetes - hypothyroidism) - common neurological diseases from birth (cerebral palsy - epilepsy) - cancer - vitiligo - common symptoms of diseases in children, and procedures for dealing with them.

ED40F.title: Graduation Project
ED40F.description: The course includes the concept of the graduation project and its objectives, the steps and methodological procedures involved, writing a specific plan for a project focused on a field problem related to teaching and learning practices, constructing data collection tools, and writing the project report.

ED40S.title: Graduation Project
ED40S.description: The course includes the concept of the graduation project and its objectives, the steps and methodological procedures involved, writing a specific plan for a project focused on a field problem related to teaching and learning practices, constructing data collection tools, and writing the project report.

ED41F.title: Action Research – Extended Course
ED41F.description: The course content includes the concept of educational research, its skills, the concept of action research, its origins, importance, and characteristics. It covers the different types of action research, the differences between action research and other types of research, models of action research, the role of reflection in each phase of the research process, the challenges associated with action research and how to address them, as well as examples of areas for action research.

ED41S.title: Action Research – Extended Course
ED41S.description: The course content includes the concept of educational research, its skills, the concept of action research, its origins, importance, and characteristics. It covers the different types of action research, the differences between action research and other types of research, models of action research, the role of reflection in each phase of the research process, the challenges associated with action research and how to address them, as well as examples of areas for action research.

EDF108.title: Active Learning Strategies
EDF108.description: The course content includes the concept of active learning and its theoretical foundations, its objectives, importance, and characteristics. It also covers models of active learning strategies and techniques such as discussion, brainstorming, collaborative learning, inquiry-based learning, scaffolding, educational games, and educational drama.

EDF213E.title: Education for Sustainable Development
EDF213E.description: The course content includes the concepts of sustainable development and its goals (Sustainable Development Goals), as well as education for sustainable development. It addresses global challenges such as climate change, environmental degradation, loss of biodiversity, poverty, and inequality. The course also focuses on how to make informed decisions and take individual and collective actions to effect change in our communities and care for our planet.

EDF226.title: Developmental psychology
EDF226.description: The course content includes the concept of developmental psychology, its objectives, its importance, the stages of growth, the characteristics of each stage, the factors affecting it, the growth needs of each age stage, the principles of growth, and some theories of growth. Such as: Piaget's and Erikson's theory, the stage of adolescence and its characteristics, some problems of childhood and adolescence, and how to overcome them.

EDF227E.title: Educational and Administrative Theories
EDF227E.description: The course content includes the concept of learning, its theories, conditions, and its relationship with emotions, motivations, and perception. It addresses individual differences in learning and achievement, memory and forgetting, and practical applications in modern psychology. The course also focuses on utilizing educational, psychological, and administrative theories to improve learning outcomes, the conditions for learning and control, types of intelligence, individual differences, the retention and transfer of learning effects, social interaction within the school, the educational climate, classroom management systems, administrative activities, and concepts related to leadership behavior.

EDF229E.title: Introduction to Positive Psychology
EDF229E.description: The course content includes an introduction to the study of positive psychology and its functions, the power of positive emotions and feelings, positive forces, positive education, self-efficacy and achievement, emotional intelligence, life satisfaction, optimism and hope, happiness, the psychology of wisdom, and readings in positive psychology research related to talent and creativity.

EDF350.title: Contemporary Trends in Psychology
EDF350.description: The course content includes some modern trends in psychology such as information processing theory of memory, cognitive strategies and learning methods, various educational models like cognitive learning: Ausubel, Bruner, Gagne, and social cognitive learning models: Rotter, Bandura. It also covers the role of cognitive processes in innovation, contemporary theories in educational psychology, mastery learning and innovation skills, and the applications of psychometric theories in daily life.

EDF351.title: Inclusion of Individuals with Special Needs
EDF351.description: The course content includes an introduction to the education and learning of individuals with special needs, types of disabilities, and the evolution of special education strategies from segregation to inclusion. It covers levels of inclusion, principles and methods of inclusion in teaching, adapting activities, and modifying the classroom environment for special education teams working with individuals with mild to moderate disabilities. Additionally, the course addresses key support programs used in mainstream schools for inclusive education, resource rooms, their concepts, and the material and human resources required, as well as assessment and evaluation methods within the inclusion system.

EDF352E.title: Alternative Assessment and Its Applications
EDF352E.description: The course content includes the concept of alternative assessment and its importance, studying the differences between traditional assessment and alternative assessment. It covers strategies and tools for alternative assessment such as student portfolios, performance-based assessment, observation, writing tests, concept mapping, and projects. It also discusses alternative assessment tools including checklists, rating scales, rubrics, and learning logs, as well as applications of alternative assessment strategies.

EDF353E.title: Education and Entrepreneurship
EDF353E.description: The course content includes an introduction to entrepreneurship, creativity and idea generation, project identification, an introduction to business plans and feasibility studies, marketing the project, identifying customers, operational planning, capital, estimating expected costs, projected income, skills for presenting entrepreneurial projects, modern trends in entrepreneurship, and the entrepreneurial environment.

EDF354E.title: E-Learning
EDF354E.description: The course content includes the concept of e-learning and related concepts such as learning resources, innovations in educational technology, their characteristics, types, classifications, and foundations for their use. It addresses the challenges of e-learning in education and strategies for overcoming these challenges, the concept of distance education, instructional design and its theories, designing teaching and learning situations in the area of specialization, social networks, educational platforms, and smart learning environments and their applications in teaching and learning.

EDS214E.title: Partnership Between Kindergarten and
EDS214E.description: The course content includes knowledge and concepts related to parenting education, the concept of partnership, its importance, objectives, areas, and the participating parties. It covers the foundations and criteria for partnership between kindergarten and school, key strategies and obstacles to effective partnerships, concepts and methods of educational support for families, and enhancing the relationship between parents and kindergarten to meet the basic, psychological, and social needs of kindergarten children.

EDS240E.title: Contemporary Trends in Teaching the Major
EDS240E.description: The course content includes modern trends in teaching the major and their relation to various learning theories, including behavioral theory, cognitive theory, and social theory. It covers teaching strategies associated with contemporary educational trends and their implementation in teaching the major, as well as evaluation methods. The course also addresses the roles of the teacher and the learner in integrated technology within the teaching and learning processes, types of digital and interactive learning resources, and their application in education. Additionally, it explores the use of augmented reality technology in education, applications of artificial intelligence in teaching, and the ethics of technology along with scientific standards for dealing with technology.

EDS242.title: Micro Teaching (2)
EDS242.description: The course content includes the concept of lesson preparation and its types, its importance, and the differences between preparation and introduction. It covers explanation techniques and their types, diversifying stimuli, verbal and non-verbal interaction, motivating students, formulating and managing questions, their levels, using educational media and tools, and evaluating learning, including its types, methods, and tools.

EDS243E.title: International Organizations and Education Development
EDS243E.description: The course content includes the importance of international organizations and their development, objectives, functions, and competencies, particularly those working in the field of education such as UNESCO, UNICEF, and the World Bank, as well as regional organizations like ALECSO and ISESCO. It covers the initiatives targeted by these organizations, such as the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs), and Egypt's commitments regarding various educational areas. The course also examines educational indicators that measure a country's ability to fulfill its obligations to these organizations, compares educational indicators among different countries, and analyzes Egypt's ranking on these indicators.

EDS362.title: Comparative and International Education
EDS362.description: The course content includes the origins of comparative education, its concept, historical development, and key pioneers. It covers the objectives of comparative education, its importance, and various fields, as well as the research methods used in comparative education. Additionally, it addresses the techniques and methods of comparative educational research, factors influencing educational policies and systems, the reciprocal relationships between educational systems and their societies, various international assessments and how to benefit from their results, contemporary issues in different educational systems, and their implications for the educational reality.

EDS363.title: School Curriculum
EDS363.description: The course content includes the concepts of traditional and modern curricula, curriculum design and development, and the various foundations for curriculum construction (philosophical, psychological, social, and cultural foundations). It covers curriculum elements (objectives, content, teaching methods and educational activities, learning resources, and assessment), curriculum organization, best global practices in school curricula, and curriculum issues in Egypt.

EDS364E.title: Reflection and Guidance in Professional Practices
EDS364E.description: The course content includes the concept of reflection, reflective practice, its importance, models, methods, and tools, as well as its relationship to metacognition and creative problem-solving in professional contexts. It also covers improving professional performance, the concept of mentorship, its significance in professional development, its areas, stages, and methods. Additionally, the course addresses the skills and roles of the mentor, the roles of the mentee, and the challenges of mentorship and how to confront them.

EDS365E.title: Specialization-Based and Interdisciplinary Education
EDS365E.description: The course content includes the concept of interdisciplinary education, its importance, characteristics, and the differences between specialization-based education and interdisciplinary education. It discusses how to activate interdisciplinary education, its objectives, strategies, and the skills necessary for its implementation. Additionally, the course covers activities and applications related to both specialization-based and interdisciplinary education, as well as issues and challenges associated with these approaches.

EDS366E.title: Multiple Intelligences
EDS366E.description: The course content includes the theory of multiple intelligences, its origins, significance, and the various types of intelligences along with their characteristics, including linguistic intelligence, logical-mathematical intelligence, spatial intelligence, bodily-kinesthetic intelligence, interpersonal intelligence, musical intelligence, intrapersonal intelligence, naturalistic intelligence, and others. The course also covers how to recognize these intelligences in learners, as well as learning strategies, activities, and educational tools suitable for each type of intelligence.

EL111.title: English Communication Skills (L4)
EL111.description: C21 English for the 21st Century is a course that combines a general English syllabus with a focus on 21st-centruy (C21) skills. These skills combine academic skills, study skills and 21st-century skills such as critical thinking, creative thinking and collaboration. The course encourages learners to develop their overall communicative skills and become independent, autonomous, and active learners. This is achieved by giving learners help and guidance through specific notes and activities. Learners are expected to provide comprehensive answers and explanations, incorporating their personal experiences and ideas in the classroom. A wide range of skills is introduced to help learners succeed in their studies and future work. Creative thinking is emphasized, enabling learners to generate solutions to various problem scenarios. Research plays an integral role in this process, requiring learners to engage with material outside the classroom. Teamwork is also highly encouraged, fostering collaboration and respect for diverse perspectives to overcome communication challenges.

EL112.title: English Communication Skills (L5)
EL112.description: The course aims to encourage learners to further develop their overall communicative abilities and become independent, autonomous learners. Learners are prompted to take a more active role in the learning process. They are given help and guidance towards this goal both through specific notes and activities and as part of an approach straddling the course. For many activities, giving simple monosyllabic yes/no answers are discouraged and learners are often encouraged to explain or support their answers. They are also asked to bring their own experiences and ideas into the classroom. Learners are introduced to a wide range of skills that will be useful to them in both their future studies and when they enter the world of work. Learners are encouraged to think about ways in which they can think and act more effectively. They also focus on how to be more creative and are often required to produce creative solutions to problems similar to those they are likely to face in the future. Research plays an important part in this process; learners will be required to do work between classes and not treat the course as simply something they do in the classroom. At the same time, learners are introduced to the various aspects of collaboration – how to work effectively with other people, showing deference to people, their views and cultures, whether they are similar or different to their own. Communicating in groups and teams is challenging. Learners are given opportunities throughout the course to develop awareness of themselves and the people they work and study with and to adapt and develop strategies that allow them to work creatively and productively while avoiding misunderstanding and conflict.

ENF101.title: Listening and Speaking
ENF101.description: Course Content: effective communication through the correct use of language, practical applications in everyday situations, and enhancing listening skills by understanding oral excerpts through recorded materials.

ENF102.title: Reading and Comprehension Strategies
ENF102.description: Course Content: the concept of reading, its stages and types, its importance, characteristics of a good reader, the definition of comprehension and its significance, reading strategies and skills, the differences between skimming and detailed reading, and the study of excerpts from reading texts.

ENF103.title: Phonetics (1)
ENF103.description: Course Content: the definition of phonetics and its importance across various fields, articulation points, analysis of linguistic sound studies, consonants and vowels, classification of sounds based on articulation location, manner, and state of vocal cords, and practice in reproducing words and sentences using phonetic symbols.

ENF104.title: Introduction to Linguistics
ENF104.description: Course Content: The nature of linguistics, its history, speech in language, the tongue, the nature of human language and its components, linguistic conflict: its causes and consequences, the various fields of linguistics, and the basic concepts in each field.

ENF105.title: Introduction to Drama and Story
ENF105.description: Course Content: The concept of the play, its distinguishing features as a literary genre different from novels and poetry, elements of the dramatic text, prose and its forms and history in the English language, and applications related to the elements of prose literature, particularly those related to storytelling.

ENF106.title: Principles of Writing and Written Translation
ENF106.description: Course Content: Key principles of writing, its skills and stages, components of sentences, types of sentences and phrases, how to use punctuation marks, and essential principles of written translation through translating several texts in various fields from English and into it, along with studying fundamental concepts of approaches

ENF107E.title: Children's Literature: Perspectives
ENF107E.description: Course Content: the concept of children's literature, its origins and development, analysis of literary texts in English for children, evaluation of these texts based on selection criteria, and the extraction of educational values from the literary text.

ENF108E.title: History of English Literature
ENF108E.description: Course Content: the nature of studying English literature (theater, novels, poetry), its roots, and its historical and cultural origins.

ENF217.title: Grammar and Language Exercises (2)
ENF217.description: Course Content: communication skills in English: their foundations, skills, and principles of communicating correctly in the language.

ENF218.title: Morphology and Syntax
ENF218.description: Course Content: the concept of the morpheme, types (roots, prefixes, suffixes), various types of suffixes from derivational to inflectional, the system of derivation, and the morphological system in English.

ENF219.title: Writing (2) (Argumentative)
ENF219.description: Course Content: the concept of argumentative writing, writing analytical and argumentative essays characterized by coherence and logical organization, and applications to enhance the ability to arrange ideas logically, adopting a scientific and literary methodology in argumentative writing, and properly documenting references.

ENF220.title: Art of Storytelling
ENF220.description: Course Content: literary trends in storytelling in the 18th century through selected novels from various novelists, along with literary criticism of the works.

ENF221.title: Drama
ENF221.description: Course Content: characteristics and elements of classical theater, study of several dramatic texts, and the literary style of Shakespeare's plays.

ENF222.title: Oral Presentation
ENF222.description: Course Content: the concept of oral presentation, its foundations, objectives, fields, and forms, skills for spontaneous speaking, presentation skills, discussions, and group debate sessions.

ENF223E.title: Reading and Writing Essays
ENF223E.description: Course Content: skills for inferring facts and perspectives from reading passages, writing analytical and argumentative essays characterized by coherence and logical organization, and adopting a scientific and literary methodology in writing.

ENF224E.title: Introduction to Linguistics
ENF224E.description: Course Content: The emergence of linguistics, its nature, the nature of human language, its components, the various fields of linguistics, and the fundamental concepts in each field.

ENF333.title: Analytical Reading
ENF333.description: Course Content: the concept of analytical reading, its skills, significance, strategies, and skills for inferring facts and perspectives from reading passages.

ENF334.title: Translation into English
ENF334.description: Course Content: characteristics of English texts, key principles of translation from Arabic to English and their applications, simultaneous and oral translation, and translating scientific, literary, and journalistic texts from Arabic to English, as well as the challenges of translating into English.

ENF335.title: Modern and Contemporary Poetry
ENF335.description: Course Content: poetry in the 20th century, its characteristics, key features, famous poets of the period, influences on their writings and thoughts, and examples of poems reflecting the era and its poetic schools.

ENF336.title: Psycholinguistics and Sociolinguistics
ENF336.description: Course Content: foundations of sociolinguistics, its methodologies and areas, especially those related to language variations, the relationship between structure, function, idea, language, age, and social and cultural context, and concepts of psycholinguistics, including the relationship between linguistic behavior and psychology, and stages of language acquisition.

ENF337.title: Discourse Analysis
ENF337.description: Course Content: fundamental concepts such as discourse, text, utterance, and speech; an introduction to text linking and its tools; semantic and logical coherence; discourse analysis; and theories of speech acts.

ENF338.title: Rhetoric
ENF338.description: Course Content: basic concepts in rhetoric, the relationship between language and context, and applications in stylistic analysis of various texts across different fields.

ENF339E.title: Multicultural American/British Literature
ENF339E.description: Course Content: definitions of multicultural American and British literature (theater, novels, poetry), its origins and development, study of various literary terms, analysis of diverse literary texts from American and multicultural British literature, and understanding the interaction between cultures and global literatures.

ENF340E.title: History of the English Language
ENF340E.description: Course Content: the nature of the English language and its historical and cultural origins.

ENGN.title: English Language
ENGN.description: The course covers the basic rules of the English language, writing formal and informal letters, constructing paragraphs using linking words and relative clauses, reviewing books, and writing postcards. Additionally, students will learn how to communicate in social situations, engage in shopping, and answer the phone. They will develop the ability to express themselves using English expressions for daily interactions and become familiar with common words and essential phrases in the language.

ENS109.title: Introduction to English Poetry
ENS109.description: Course Content: Basic terms related to English poetry, the history of English poetry, various forms of poetry, differences among them, and analysis of different poetic texts from important works by several poets.

ENS110.title: Language Exercises (1
ENS110.description: Course Content: using English vocabulary and structures through exercises designed to promote correct usage of words, phrases, and idiomatic expressions, as well as improving writing and speaking skills.

ENS111.title: Writing (1) (Descriptive and Narrative)
ENS111.description: Course Content: the concept of descriptive and narrative writing, crafting a variety of grammatically correct sentences into coherent paragraphs, and professionally handling scientific data and information in English.

ENS112.title: Introduction to Literary Criticism
ENS112.description: Course Content: The concept of literary criticism, important terms related to literary criticism and their differences, and highlighting the fundamental changes in criticism through significant critics and theorists in the history and fields of literary criticism and their directions.

ENS113.title: Grammar (1)
ENS113.description: Course Content: essential rules of English grammar and morphology, basic structures in English, nominal and adverbial phrases, and various tenses.

ENS114.title: Phonetics (2)
ENS114.description: Course Content: the concept of the syllable, types of syllables, their notation, nature of diphthongs, classification, characteristics distinguishing them from vowels, intonation, and its types.

ENS115E.title: Media and Journalistic Discourse
ENS115E.description: Course Content: components of media discourse, its characteristics, schools of media discourse, its tools and challenges, with practical applications through various examples.

ENS116E.title: Integrated Language Skills
ENS116E.description: Course Content: Study of integrated language skills, communication skills in English, and training students on practical foundations for communicating in correct English.

ENS225.title: Shakespeare
ENS225.description: Course Content: an introduction to the famous English writer Shakespeare through a selection of his comedies, tragedies, and historical plays, understanding his approach to building plays, characters, and ideas, as well as the social, political, and cultural conditions that contributed to his genius, along with the study of his most notable poems.

ENS226.title: Translation into Arabic
ENS226.description: Course Content: characteristics of the Arabic language, key principles of translation from English to Arabic and their applications, simultaneous and oral translation, and translating scientific, literary, and journalistic texts from English to Arabic, as well as the challenges of translating into Arabic.

ENS227.title: Critical Reading
ENS227.description: Course Content: critical reading skills, skills for thinking about what the text says, describes, and means through examining writing style, structure, content, and language used

ENS228.title: Romantic and Victorian Poetry
ENS228.description: Course Content: the art of Romantic and Victorian poetry in the 19th century, its characteristics, key features, famous poets of the period, influences on their writings and thoughts, and the study of representative poems from this era and their schools.

ENS229.title: Contrastive Analysis and Error Analysis
ENS229.description: Course Content: the theory of linguistic contrast versus error analysis, the role of each in foreign language teaching, their importance for foreign language teachers, the causes of errors in foreign languages in general and in Arabic specifically, and applications for analyzing language errors made by learners of Arabic who are native speakers of other languages.

ENS230.title: 19th Century Novel
ENS230.description: Course Content: novels from the 19th century, analysis of literary trends in novel writing during that period, and training in analyzing literary themes and their components, including artistic styles and their application.

ENS231E.title: Rhetoric and Composition
ENS231E.description: Course Content: the importance of rhetoric and its rules, the artistic features of literary texts, essential skills such as discourse, text, utterance, and speech, an introduction to text linking and its tools, semantic and logical coherence, and discourse, along with theories of speech acts.

ENS232E.title: Western Civilization
ENS232E.description: Course Content: examining the political, social, economic, and cultural developments in Western society during the 19th and 20th centuries, as well as understanding the factors that influenced poetry, prose, and theater during these two centuries.

ENS341.title: Advanced Writing
ENS341.description: Course Content: foundations, objectives, significance, and stages of constructive writing, with applications for writing cohesive and interconnected essays by relying on scientific and literary methodology, and training on proper documentation of references.

ENS342.title: Comparative Literature
ENS342.description: Course Content: the concept of comparative literature, its fields, importance, history, trends, and the interaction between different global literatures, as well as understanding the position of Arabic literature within this context. The course seeks to reveal the significance of influence and interaction between various cultures and literatures.

ENS343.title: 20th Century Drama
ENS343.description: Course Content: an introduction to modern theater in the 20th century, its various schools such as absurd theater and symbolic theater, and developments in modern dramatic art.

ENS344.title: Semantics and Pragmatics
ENS344.description: Course Content: the origin and evolution of semantics, the relationship of semantics to linguistic sciences, the significance of semantics in levels of linguistic study, the connection between semantics and semiotics, types of linguistic meanings (phonetic, morphological, syntactic, lexical, contextual), pragmatic meaning, and its relationship to social and cultural context.

ENS345.title: Modern Criticism
ENS345.description: Course Content: The concept of literary criticism in the modern era (the twentieth century and contemporary), important terms related to literary criticism in the modern era, their differences, and highlighting the fundamental changes in criticism through showcasing critics and theorists active in the history and fields of literary criticism and their directions.

ENS346.title: Modern and Contemporary Novel
ENS346.description: Course Content: the concept of the novel, modern and contemporary novels, the essential elements of a novel, analysis of novels from the 20th century and modern times in English and American literature, literary trends in contemporary novel writing across various themes, and the emergence of new types of novels that reinvent myths to express modern topics within a unique framework.

ENS347E.title: Advanced Grammar
ENS347E.description: Course Content: studying the most important advanced rules of English grammar and morphology, as well as basic and advanced grammatical structures, nominal and adverbial phrases, and various tenses.

ENS348E.title: Applied Linguistics
ENS348E.description: Course Content:: studying concepts of applied linguistics, communication skills in English: their foundations, skills, and applications of effective communication in the language.

FTF32.title: Field Training (2)
FTF32.description: The practices of the course include analyzing textbooks in the area of specialization, utilizing relevant resources, preparing daily lesson plans, selecting educational and learning media, and assessment tools, participating in school activities, collaborating with peers, interacting with students, teachers, and school administration, reflecting on field training practices, participating in discussion groups to evaluate their effectiveness, as well as engaging positively with the guidance of field training supervisors.

FTF44.title: Field Training (4)
FTF44.description: The practices of the course include analyzing textbooks in the area of specialization, utilizing relevant resources, preparing daily lesson plans, selecting educational and learning media, and assessment tools, participating in school activities, collaborating with peers, interacting with students, teachers, and school administration, reflecting on field training practices, participating in discussion groups to evaluate their effectiveness, as well as engaging positively with the guidance of field training supervisors.

FTS33.title: Field Training (3)
FTS33.description: The practices of the course include analyzing textbooks in the area of specialization, utilizing relevant resources, preparing daily lesson plans, selecting educational and learning media, and assessment tools, participating in school activities, collaborating with peers, interacting with students, teachers, and school administration, reflecting on field training practices, participating in discussion groups to evaluate their effectiveness, as well as engaging positively with the guidance of field training supervisors.

FTS45.title: Field Training (5)
FTS45.description: The practices of the course include analyzing textbooks in the area of specialization, utilizing relevant resources, preparing daily lesson plans, selecting educational and learning media, and assessment tools, participating in school activities, collaborating with peers, interacting with students, teachers, and school administration, reflecting on field training practices, participating in discussion groups to evaluate their effectiveness, as well as engaging positively with the guidance of field training supervisors.

GR 101.title: Self Learning Skills
GR 101.description: This Course aims at providing students with the necessary knowledge for self-learning and its psychological educational foundations that will provide students with a number of practical skills such as understanding, thinking, information processing, reading and writing, besides dealing with the information and self-learning technological skills, in addition to the adoption of self-learning strategies for life.

GR 111.title: Arabic-Islamic Civilization
GR 111.description: This course looks at an overall view in the history of the Arabic-Islamic Civilization. This includes the exploration of several concepts and social issues, as well as Islamic arts and architecture.

GR 112.title: Issues and Problems of Development in the Arab World
GR 112.description: This course introduces students to the study of development, specifically looking at the status of human development in the Arab World and its social indicators.

GR 118.title: Life skills and Coexistence
GR 118.description: This course enables individuals to develop their positive and adaptive behaviors to effectively deal with the requirements and challenges of life. It aims at helping students to acquire skills such as: effective communication, problem solving, stress management and leadership. It also deals with issues such as: human and women rights, democracy, accepting others and tolerance.

GR 121.title: Environment and Health
GR 121.description: The course focuses on introduction social and natural sciences which study the relationship between human activity and human environment. Looking at various topics using a case-study approach.

GR 131.title: History and Civilization of AOU branch country
GR 131.description: This course introduces students to the historical background of the AOU branch country, its political, socioeconomic development and democratic experience.

GR111.title: Arabic Islamic Civilization
GR111.description: This course aims to provide students with knowledge of the achievements of Islamic civilization and its impact on Western civilization during the Middle Ages through a series of objectives associated with each unit.

GR112.title: Issues and Problems of Development in the Arab Region
GR112.description: GR112 deals with issues and problems related to the development of the Arab region, specifically human development and its social indicators, Arab culture, education, mass media, health, nutrition, women, environment and natural resources.

GR118.title: Life Skills and Coexistence
GR118.description: This course deals with the abilities that enable individuals to engage in adaptive and positive behavior that makes them able to deal effectively with life's demands and challenges. It seeks to know the concept of skill and how to acquire and develop it, such as the skill of developing self-awareness, managing psychological stress, effective communication, solving problems and conflicts, leadership, and building work teams, in addition to presenting topics in pluralism and democracy, women’s rights, the subject of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, and acceptance of... The other, coexistence and tolerance.

GR118E.title: Life Skills and Coexistence
GR118E.description: This course aims to develop Academic, self, and communication skills among Arab Open university students, and applying these skills in their practical and university life, the matter that will contribute in enhancing student`s abilities and skills improvement together with other courses that the university provides to develop their cognitive aspect.

GR131.title: Branch Requirement Course
GR131.description: GR131 introduces students to current issues of interest to socio-economic development at the local and regional levels.

GR131E.title: Egyptian Society: History, Civilization, and Future
GR131E.description: The course aims to familiarize students with various aspects of Egyptian society historically, culturally, and in terms of values and development. This is crucial for students at this stage of life to understand their surrounding society, comprehend reality, connect it with the past, and relate to the cultural and value characteristics of Egyptians throughout history. This foundation is intended to direct their energy towards playing an active role in building society, correcting its negatives, and participating in development, inspired by the achievements of their great ancestors and the quality education they receive at the university. Specifically, the course aims to introduce students to ancient Egyptian civilization, its creative aspects, and the features of life in ancient Egyptian society. The course then covers cultural capital in Egyptian society, explaining the pillars, components, manifestations, and aspects of Egyptian culture. It also addresses Egyptian value capital and the significant value transformations that the Egyptian personality has undergone. The course then guides students on their role in the development process and introduces them to a range of developmental terms such as sustainable development, development maps, and development paths. It clarifies the roles of the state and various entities like universities, media, and civil society in implementing the development map, linking all these aspects to the actual reality of Egyptian society striving for successful development as part of Egypt's 2030 Strategic plan.

MAF101.title: General Chemistry
MAF101.description: This course includes the following content:Introduction to chemistry and its importance, Steps of chemical analysis,Types of chemical solutions and how to calculate their concentrations,pH value and measurement methods,Titrations and their types,Equivalence point and end point,Methods for calculating the activity coefficient and the effect of ions,Classification of acids and bases,Calculating the pH of weak polyprotic acids and bases,Calculating the pH of salt solutions,Saturated hydrocarbons,Unsaturated hydrocarbons,Alkynes,Aromatic

MAF102.title: Introduction to Statistics
MAF102.description: This course covers: data tabulation and classification, construction of graphical representations, significance level, measures of central tendency, measures of dispersion, coefficient of variation, correlation coefficient, and both Spearman and Pearson methods

MAF103.title: Dynamics1
MAF103.description: The course's scientific content includes: Axioms of Mechanics - Motion of a Body in a Resisting Medium - Motion in a Vertical Circle - Vertical and Circular Motion - Vectors - Composition and Resolution of Forces - Equilibrium of a Particle in a Plane and in Space - Pappus-Guldinus Theorems - Rigid Body - Differentiation of Vectors: Velocity and Acceleration - Harmonic Motion - Circular Motion - Momentum - Energy - Power

MAF104.title: Statics1
MAF104.description: The scientific content of this course includes: vector algebra, types of forces, moments, couples, equivalence of force systems, equilibrium of bodies in 2D and 3D, equilibrium of structures, and internal forces in beams (shear forces and bending moments). It also covers trusses, equilibrium of heavy cables and distributed loads, and center of gravity (for wires, areas, and volumes). Further topics include moment of inertia and products of inertia, the parallel axis theorem, rotation of axes and principal moments of inertia, virtual work and stability of equilibrium, and an introduction to fluid statics.

MAF105.title: Analytical Geometry 1
MAF105.description: The course content includes: vectors in the plane, the straight line, conic sections, parametric equations of curves in the plane (cycloid, and conic sections), the general second-degree equation in two variables, vectors in space, the distance from a point to a plane, surfaces of revolution, the equation of a straight line, and the plane.

MAF106.title: Properties of matter and temperature
MAF106.description: The course's scientific content covers two main areas: Properties of Matter and Heat. Under Properties of Matter, topics include dimensional analysis and its applications, elasticity and its coefficients, surface tension and capillarity, hydrodynamics, fluid motion including Bernoulli's equation and its practical applications, viscosity, diffusion, and osmotic pressure. The Heat section begins with an introduction to the concepts of heat, temperature, and thermal equilibrium, followed by the mechanical equivalent of heat, thermometers, and temperature scales. It also delves into the effect of heat on materials, covering phase transformations, thermal expansion and its applications, the anomalous behavior of water, thermal stresses, and discoloration. Finally, it explores the mechanisms of heat transfer, specifically thermal insulation of buildings and thermal conduction.

MAF107E.title: Introduction to Algebra
MAF107E.description: This course includes the following topics: Introduction to mathematical logic, sets, Cartesian product, relations and mappings, algebraic systems and binary operations, definitions of group, ring, and field, residue classes, partial fractions, mathematical induction, summation of finite series, convergence and divergence of infinite series, binomial theorem expansions, higher-order determinants, solving systems of linear equations, matrix algebra, and complex number algebra

MAF108E.title: Introduction to Computer Science
MAF108E.description: This course covers: an introduction to computers, computer components, operating systems, an introduction to computer networks and the internet, computer viruses, utilization of computers in various sectors of society, practical applications using Windows OS, Microsoft Word (word processor), Microsoft Excel (spreadsheets), Microsoft Access (database), Microsoft PowerPoint (presentations), Internet Explorer (web browser), and antivirus software.

MAF217.title: Philosophy and History of Mathematics
MAF217.description: The course's scientific content includes: Philosophy and Nature of Mathematics - The Interrelation between Philosophy and Mathematics - Mathematics in Babylonian and Ancient Egyptian Civilizations - Contributions of Indians and Chinese - Mathematics among the Greeks - Development of Mathematics in Arabic and Islamic Civilizations - Mathematics and the European Renaissance - Invention of Analytical Geometry and Calculus in the 17th and 18th Centuries - Mathematics in the 19th Century - Non-Euclidean Geometry - Set Theory and Abstract Algebra - Characteristics of Mathematics in the 20th Century.

MAF218.title: Group Theory
MAF218.description: The course content includes: the concept of a group, types of groups (subgroups, cyclic groups), Lagrange's Theorem, normal subgroups, quotient groups, group homomorphisms, isomorphism theorems, automorphisms of groups, simple groups, Cayley's Theorem and its generalization, symmetry groups, group action on a set, Cauchy's Theorem, Sylow's Theorems and their applications, direct products, and classification of small order groups up to isomorphism

MAF219.title: Calculus 2
MAF219.description: The course's scientific content includes: Indefinite Integral - Properties of Integration - Integration of Trigonometric Functions - Integration of Inverse Trigonometric Functions - Integration of Exponential Functions - Integration of Logarithmic Functions - Integration of Hyperbolic Functions - Integration of Inverse Hyperbolic Functions - Integration by Partial Fractions - Integration by Parts - Integration by Substitution - Substitution using Algebraic Functions - Substitution using Trigonometric Functions - Integration by Reduction - Deriving General Formulas for the Reduction of: Trigonometric Functions and Hyperbolic Functions - Properties of the Definite Integral - Improper Integral - Using Definite Integral to Find Area - Volumes of Revolution - Finding the Volume of a Sphere - Surface Areas of Revolution - Surface Area of a Sphere.

MAF220.title: Real Analysis
MAF220.description: The scientific content of this course includes: fundamental properties of the real number line, the completeness axiom, countable sets, the Bolzano-Weierstrass Theorem, and Cauchy's application. It also covers the basic properties of the topology of real numbers, a study of limits of functions, proving facts about limits, as well as continuity and uniform continuity and the differences between them. The course defines the Riemann integral, Darboux's Theorem and Riemann sums, the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, sequences and series of functions, pointwise convergence, and uniform convergence

MAF221.title: Analytical Geometry 2
MAF221.description: The course content includes: coordinate systems (Cartesian and polar coordinates), various forms of equations for a straight line in the plane, the equation of a tangent to a curve in the plane, pairs of straight lines, various forms of the equation of a circle, conic sections (their physical and geometric properties, and methods of drawing them), the polar form of conic sections, and equations of tangents to conic sections.

MAF222.title: Numerical Analysis
MAF222.description: The scientific content of this course includes: an introduction to numerical analysis, error estimation, solving non-linear equations, interpolation, theories for validating results, numerical integration and differentiation, solving systems of linear equations, matrix analysis methods, an introduction to solving ordinary differential equations, and Gaussian quadratures

MAF223E.title: Multimedia Mechanics
MAF223E.description: The course content includes: mechanical extensors and their types, Kayla's theory, extensor fields, stress analysis, fracture and strain, current flow, fundamental laws of continuum mechanics, and applications to viscosity and fluidity

MAF224E.title: Mathematical Analysis
MAF224E.description: The scientific content of this course includes: inverse functions, derivatives of inverse functions, derivatives of hyperbolic, inverse hyperbolic, and inverse trigonometric functions, and the relationship between inverse hyperbolic functions and the logarithmic function. It also covers various forms of L'Hôpital's Rule for limits. Integration methods include integration by substitution, by parts, and by partial fractions, along with applications of definite integrals. The course then moves to functions of several variables, partial derivatives, the chain rule, the equation of the tangent plane to a surface and its normal line, maxima and minima, and Taylor and Maclaurin expansions in two variables. Finally, it covers multiple integrals: double and triple integrals in Cartesian and polar coordinates, and triple integrals in Cartesian, cylindrical, and spherical coordinates

MAF333.title: Fluids
MAF333.description: This course delves into fluid statics, beginning with the main equation of fluid statics and exploring static forces on submerged planar and curved surfaces. It then transitions to fluid dynamics, introducing Lagrangian and Eulerian systems and analyzing particle derivatives and acceleration in both Cartesian and cylindrical coordinate systems. Key concepts like streamlines, pathlines, and streaklines are covered, leading into fundamental principles such as Bernoulli's theorem and the calculation of dynamic fluid pressure. Practical applications, including the Pitot tube and Venturi meter, are discussed alongside the essential continuity and motion equations. Further topics include vorticity and circulation, Stokes' flow equation, and the use of the complex potential function to understand phenomena like sources, sinks, and their duality. The course concludes with advanced concepts such as the circle theorem and Blasius' theorem

MAF334.title: Software for Mathematical and Statistical Applications
MAF334.description: The scientific content of this course includes: an introduction to symbolic computational software packages (e.g., Mathematica), an introduction to numerical computational software packages (e.g., MATLAB, SPSS), the use of computer programs in calculus and differential equations, and the application of numerical computation software to solve problems in numerical analysis.

MAF335.title: Ring and Field Theories
MAF335.description: The course content includes: the concept of a ring and subring (their properties and examples), ring homomorphism and isomorphism, integral domains and fields, the field of quotients of an integral domain (the rational field of an integral domain), prime fields and the characteristic of a ring, polynomial rings (division and greatest common divisor), roots of polynomials over a field, ideals and quotient rings, direct sums of rings and their properties, ring spaces and Euclidean rings, field extensions (simple and finite extensions of fields), algebraic closure of a field, splitting fields, and finite fields.

MAF336.title: Linear Algebra
MAF336.description: The course's scientific content includes: Systems of Linear Equations and Matrices - Vectors in Two and Three Dimensions - General Vector Space - Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors - Matrix Diagonalization - Quadratic Form of Equations and Their Transformation to Canonical Form - Vector Spaces - Linear Independence - Dimensions and Basis Vectors of Spaces - Basis Transformation - Dot Product - Orthogonal Vectors - Linear Transformations, and their Applications

MAF337.title: Functional Analysis
MAF337.description: The scientific content of this course includes: metric spaces and fundamental inequalities. It covers open and closed sets, convergence, spherical neighborhoods, closure of a set and its properties, and complete metric spaces. The course then moves to normed spaces, subspaces of a normed space, and equivalent norms. Regarding linear operators on a normed space, it defines the linear, continuous, and bounded operator, linear operators on finite-dimensional spaces, and the inverse of a linear operator. Finally, it covers inner product spaces and Hilbert spaces, orthogonal sets, the Riesz Representation Theorem, properties of linear and bounded operators between Hilbert spaces, and adjoint, self-adjoint, normal, and unitary operators

MAF338.title: Quantum Mechanics
MAF338.description: The course content includes: wave-particle duality, wave packets, solving the Schrödinger equation for a free particle, solving the Schrödinger equation for a bound particle, quantum postulates, matrix mechanics, angular momentum, and spin.

MAF339E.title: Probability and Statistics
MAF339E.description: This course covers fundamental concepts in statistics and probability, beginning with data organization, summarization, and presentation through tables, including relative and percentage frequency tables for both qualitative and quantitative data. It then delves into graphical representation for both types of data, followed by an exploration of measures of central tendency, percentiles, and dispersion. The course also introduces the principles of probability, covering concepts such as sets, statistical experiments, sample space, events, operations on events, mutually exclusive events, exhaustive events, and equally likely outcomes. Further topics include conditional probability, independent events, the definition of a random variable, selected discrete probability distributions, and the normal distribution, concluding with an introduction to correlation and regression

MAF340E.title: Electromagnetic Theory
MAF340E.description: The course content includes: electrostatic fields, their equations, and Gauss's Law in vacuum and dielectric materials; an introduction to conservative force fields, potential energy, and a study of electrostatic potential, Laplace's and Poisson's equations and their solutions; magnetic fields and their calculation, and Ampere's Law for magnetostatics; time-varying fields, Maxwell's equations, and the Law of Conservation of Charge; solving Maxwell's equations in vacuum, the propagation of electromagnetic waves in various media, magnetic power, the Poynting vector, and the electromagnetic wave spectrum

MAS109.title: Algebra
MAS109.description: The course's scientific content includes: Group Theory - Subgroups - Group Homomorphisms - Permutation Groups - Cyclic Groups - Group Isomorphism, and Quotient Groups - Geometric Transformation Groups - Rings, Ideals, and Quotient Rings - Subfields and Field Factorization - Algebraically Closed Fields - Integral Domains - Polynomials over a Field

MAS110.title: Calculus1
MAS110.description: This course's content includes: the concept of a function, its properties, operations on functions, types of functions, function composition, and inverse functions. It covers the concept of limits, properties of limits, the concept of a function's limit at infinity, and the concept of right-hand and left-hand limits, along with methods for calculating limits. The course also delves into the concept of continuity, its properties, and theorems on continuity. Furthermore, it examines the concept of differentiation, the relationship between differentiation and continuity, differentiation rules, trigonometric functions, derivatives of inverse trigonometric functions, hyperbolic functions, derivatives of inverse hyperbolic functions, derivatives of exponential and logarithmic functions, higher-order derivatives and Leibniz's Theorem, the chain rule, implicit differentiation, and parametric forms of functions, along with a study of some applications of differentiation. Finally, the course covers integration: integration of algebraic functions, integration of exponential and logarithmic functions, integration of trigonometric and inverse trigonometric functions, and integration of hyperbolic and inverse hyperbolic functions

MAS111.title: Dynamics2
MAS111.description: The course's scientific content includes: Review of Simple Harmonic Motion - Damped Harmonic Motion - Examples and Applications of Damped Harmonic Motion - Central Orbits - Applications of Central Orbits - Kepler's Laws - Introduction to Space Dynamics - Circular Coordinate Systems - Motion Near the Earth's Surface and Foucault's Pendulum - Velocity and Acceleration in Circular Systems in Cylindrical Coordinates - Velocity and Acceleration in Circular Systems in Polar and Spherical Coordinates.

MAS112.title: Statics 2
MAS112.description: The scientific content of this course includes: spatial statics, friction force and normal reaction, slipping and overturning, center of gravity, virtual work, stability of equilibrium, and reduction of force systems.

MAS113.title: Introduction to Number Theory and logic
MAS113.description: This course covers: numerical identities – linear congruence and the theory of residues – primitive roots and indices – quadratic residues, Legendre symbol, and the law of quadratic reciprocity – arithmetic functions – basic Diophantine equations – infinite continued fractions and rational approximations of real numbers – Pell’s equation – distribution of prime numbers

MAS114.title: Electricity, Magnetism and Alternating Current
MAS114.description: The course content includes: Coulomb’s law, Gauss’s theorem, electric field and lines of force, equipotential surface, electric dipole, Poisson’s and Laplace’s equations, Poisson transformations, solving Laplace equations, and the continuity equation.

MAS115E.title: Graph Theory
MAS115E.description: The course content includes: an introduction to Graph Theory, applications of the theory, vector forms/shapes, basic concepts and theories about forms/shapes, algorithms, shape theory, and computer programs.

MAS116E.title: Space Mechanics and Astronomy
MAS116E.description: The course content includes: an introduction to planetary mechanics and its applications, the motion of artificial satellites and spacecraft in space, orbital elements, converting orbital elements into position and velocity vectors, types of space orbits, and space orbit design.

MAS225.title: Topology
MAS225.description: The scientific content of this course includes: the concept of topology, definitions of topological spaces, closed and open sets, interior and boundary regions, first and second countability axioms, separable spaces, methods of generating topology on sets, interior and closure operators, bases and sub-bases, subspaces, Cartesian products, sums, embedding, local embedding, and metrizable topological spaces.

MAS226.title: Spherical Geometry
MAS226.description: The course content includes: vectors in space, various forms of the equation of a straight line in space, the vector and parametric equations of a space curve, the relationship between two straight lines in space (parallelism, intersection, skew lines), the equation of a plane in space, the equation of a family of planes, the relationship between a straight line and a plane, the intersection of two planes in space, equations of surfaces of revolution in space (solids of conic surfaces, the sphere, the cone), and the intersection of planes with space surfaces

MAS227.title: Calculus Equations
MAS227.description: The course includes the following topics: solving second-order differential equations, Bessel and Legendre equations, Laplace transform method, systems of equations, existence and uniqueness theorems for first- and second-order differential equations, finite difference equations, and first-order partial differential equations.

MAS228.title: Physical Chemistry
MAS228.description: The course covers the following topics: the concept of system and surroundings, types of systems, types of processes in thermodynamics (isothermal and adiabatic processes), extensive and intensive properties, the concept of free energy, enthalpy, and entropy, the zeroth law of thermodynamics and the reason behind its name, the first law of thermodynamics, work, the relationship between CVC_VCV and CPC_PCP, Hess's law, entropy as a state function, laws of chemical kinetics, rate laws, calculation of reaction rates and rate constants, rate expressions, stoichiometric measurements, reaction order, concentration profiles for reactions, integrated rate equations for simple reactions, quantitative studies of half-life times for different reactions, pseudo-order reactions, zero-order reactions, and general order reactions

MAS229.title: Calculus3
MAS229.description: The course's scientific content includes: Cartesian, Cylindrical, and Spherical Coordinates - Functions of Two Variables - Functions of Three Variables - Limits - Continuity - Partial Derivatives - Chain Rule - Extreme Values of Functions of Two Variables - Lagrange Multipliers - Double Integrals and their Applications - Double Integrals in Polar Coordinates - Triple Integrals and their Applications - Triple Integrals in Cylindrical and Spherical Coordinates - Sequences - Infinite Series - Convergence Tests - Representation of Functions by Power Series - Taylor and Maclaurin Series, and Binomial Series.

MAS230.title: Analytical Dynamics
MAS230.description: The course's scientific content includes: Basic Concepts in Analytical Dynamics - Lagrange's Equations for Holonomic Dynamical Systems - Derivation of Lagrange's Equations and Definition of the Lagrangian Function - Atwood Machine and Real-Life Applications - Hamilton's Function and Derivation of Hamilton's Equations - Jacobi Integrals and Hamilton's Principle - Derivation of Hamilton's Equations using Hamilton's Principle - Poisson Brackets - Proof of Jacobi-Poisson Theorem - Equilibrium Position

MAS231E.title: statistical Analysis
MAS231E.description: The scientific content of this course includes: sampling distributions and the Central Limit Theorem. It covers point estimation and the properties of estimators (unbiasedness, mean squared error, consistency, sufficiency, minimal sufficiency). The course also delves into the exponential family, the Cramér-Rao inequality, Fisher information, the Rao-Blackwell Theorem (sufficiency and completeness), and the Lehmann-Scheffé Theorem. Estimation methods covered include the method of moments and maximum likelihood estimators with their asymptotic properties. It also explores the use of prior density functions, invariance methods, interval estimation, confidence interval estimators, pivotal methods, and Bayesian credible intervals.

MAS232E.title: Inferential Statistics
MAS232E.description: This course's scientific content includes: the concept of inferential statistics; sampling theory, its importance and applications in society; the normal distribution and standard normal distribution, along with the table of critical values for the standard normal distribution. It also covers the chi-square distribution, theories explaining its relationship to the normal distribution, applied examples, and its critical values table. The course introduces the t-distribution, theories explaining its relationship to the normal distribution, applied examples, and its values table. Additionally, it examines the F-distribution, theories explaining its relationship to the normal distribution, applied examples, and its values table. Key topics also include the definition, importance, and practical applications of hypothesis testing, specifically chi-square, t-tests, and F-tests. Finally, the course defines simple and complex analysis of variance and simple linear regression.

MAS341.title: Complex Analysis
MAS341.description: The scientific content of this course includes: complex numbers, polar representation, complex functions, limits, continuity, analytic functions, elementary complex functions (trigonometric, hyperbolic, exponential, logarithmic, and complex power functions), differentiation, definite integrals, complex line integrals, infinite series, Taylor series, Laurent series, Residue Theorem, applications in real and improper integrals, and physical and engineering applications, as well as Cauchy's Integral Theorem.

MAS342.title: Operation Research
MAS342.description: The scientific content of this course includes: linear programming (graphical and algebraic methods, the simplex method, dual simplex method, and parametric analysis), error analysis, transportation problems and the transportation model, and integer programming (cutting plane method, linear analysis, branch and bound method). It also covers dynamic programming and various solution methods using dynamic programming.

MAS343.title: Biomathematics
MAS343.description: The course's scientific content includes: Biomathematics: Concept and Importance - Mathematical Modeling - Dynamical Systems as Differential Equations - Optimal Formulas for Solutions of Dynamical Differential Equations - Growth Equations - Competition for Fixed Resources - Applications of Exponential Functions in Biology - Time-Concentration Curves in Blood Injected with Drugs via Separation - Common Growth Functions - Exponential Curves - Time Period for Retaining Carbon Dioxide in the Lungs During Respiration - Measurement of Cardiac Output - Communication Science and Insufficiency - Differential Equations for Epidemics - Bacteriology - Mechanism of Reproduction and Extinction - Membrane Diffusion

MAS344.title: English Readings in the Specialty
MAS344.description: The scientific content of this course includes: periodic functions – binary functions – monotonic functions – limits – chain rule – mean value theorem – Leibniz’s theorem – Taylor series – Maclaurin series – homogeneous functions – Euler’s theorem for homogeneous functions – improper integrals – sets – subsets – cyclic groups – groups – Lagrange’s theorem – group symmetries – vectors – scalar product – rigid body – moments – couples – equilibrium – center of gravity – vector operators (gradient of a scalar function, divergence of a vector field, curl of a vector) – Stokes' theorem – velocity – acceleration – relative velocity – impulse – driving force – polar coordinates – simple harmonic motion – sample space – events – probability – permutations – combinations – conditional probability

MAS345.title: Integral Equations
MAS345.description: The course covers physical and mechanical problems and integral equations, linear integral equations, classification and solutions of differential and integral equations, Fredholm integral equations of the first and second kind, Volterra integral equations of the first and second kind, characteristic behavior of integral equations, and applications to ordinary differential equations.

MAS347E.title: Calculus Geometry
MAS347E.description: The course content includes: Local Curve Theory: curvature, torsion, Serret-Frenet formulas (or Frenet-Serret theory), existence and uniqueness theorem for curves. Plane Curves: non-isometric, four-vertex theorem, rotation. Local Surface Theory: first fundamental form, normal and geodesic curvature, parallelism, second fundamental form, Weingarten maps, types of curvature, and constant curvature surfaces.

MAS348E.title: Theory of Relativity
MAS348E.description: The course content includes: Introduction to Special Relativity, postulates of Special Relativity and Lorentz transformations, relativistic kinematics, geometrical representation of Special Relativity and Minkowski space, relativistic mechanics, Einstein's energy equation and various results, applications of Special Relativity (mechanical applications, applications in modern physics, and applications in chemistry)

MATS346E.title: Elasticity
MATS346E.description: The course includes the following topics: fundamental concepts, stress theory, equilibrium equations, principal stress surfaces, stress theory, stress conditions, fundamental stress components, strain energy, the relationship between stress and strain components (Hooke’s Law), fundamental problems in elasticity, Lame’s equations, Beltrami’s equations, plane stress, and plane strain.

TECN.title: Information and Communication Technologies in Education and Research
TECN.description: The course covers the principles of computer science, concepts of e-learning, and interaction with the university's educational platforms such as Learning Management Systems (LMS) and Student Information Systems (SIS). It aims to enhance students' skills and abilities to communicate effectively online and complete academic assignments. The course also includes concepts of artificial intelligence, the Internet of Things, and cybersecurity, as well as the use of the internet in education and scientific research.

AR111.title: Arabic Communication Skills (I)
AR111.description: AR111 is three credit hour university requirements. It aims to enable students to acquire the Arabic language skills needed at university level, specifically: Arabic syntactic structures, grammatical inflection and case ending in spoken and written Arabic, ability to read Arabic texts in different disciplines, adequate training in writing and using dictionary

AR112.title: Arabic Communication Skills (II)
AR112.description: AR112 is a three credit hour university requirement. It aims at developing students’ skills in text analysis and literary appreciation. Students are introduced to the principles of accurate pronunciation and sound reading of texts. The course also provides training in Arabic rhetoric and literary genres.

AR113.title: مهارات التواصل في اللغة العربية
AR113.description: تنمية الحسّ اللغوي والإلمام بالمهارات اللغوية الأربع في اللغة العربية (استماع وقراءة وكتابة وتحدث)، وتطبيق استخدامها بشكل صحيح في الحياة العامة وفي مكان العمل، بصورة تعزز مكتسبات الطالب الثقافية واللغوية والمعرفية بما يتلاءم مع بقية المواد المدروسة ضمن برنامج البكالوريوس..

B861.title: Investment and portfolio management
B861.description: This course is an elective for the direct entrants to the Finance track of the MBA programme. The scope of this course relates to an overview of theory and practice in the field of investment management which is a highly successful and diverse sector in the global economy. The overall aim of this course is to introduce the participant to the world of investments by providing the necessary theoretical knowledge, and analytical skills to evaluate different investment alternatives and enable them to construct optimal portfolios in a risk-return sense, including the use of derivatives. This includes bonds, equities, and alternative investments. It will also provide an understanding of the key factors affecting investment decision making, such as investment objectives and constraints, behavioural and ethical issues, and an understanding of the different institutions involved in portfolio management. Overall this course will build an understanding of the complex aspects of investments and portfolio management which is an increasingly important area in the study of finance.

B863.title: The Human Resource Professional
B863.description: B863 is a postgraduate course and is one of a series of optional courses offered to all students who progress to Stage II of the AOU MBA program/ mandatory for those who are to specialize in human resource management. This module will consider the role and contribution of the HR professional and the skills needed to be effective in this role. Students will consider the implications of recent research findings in the field of human resource management for their own practice, for example in increasing levels of engagement and improving performance, in acting ethically and in managing change. They will compare this with the practice of HR professionals in other contexts, drawing on case studies and the experience of their fellow students working in different geographical areas and sectors; and they will also look at the development over time of thinking about the role of HR professionals in order to understand how this may influence current thinking. The emphasis throughout will be on considering what HRM practices are associated with positive organizational outcomes. Students will develop and practice the skills they will need to be effective as an HR professional, including as a leader and a senior manager. These include self-management, leading and working in teams, making decisions, managing and communicating information, including financial information, consultancy skills and helping others to learn. They will also develop postgraduate study skills and digital literacy skills. Perhaps most importantly this module will develop students’’ skills as a reflective practitioner, committed to continuously learning from reflection on their practice and on the critical application of new theories and ideas to inform this practice. Collaboration skills of the students with all functional areas of an organization (accounting, human resources, operations, production, marketing, information technology, etc.) will be improved.

B864.title: Human resource management in context
B864.description: In this module you will examine how HR policies and practices operate within multiple tiers and manifestations of economic, political and social context - at macro (societal and international) and micro (organisational) levels. In addition to developing analytical and practical skills in this specific domain, the module breaks new ground by incorporating resourcing and talent management as extended examples of HR practice and to illustrate how an intelligent understanding and reading of context by skilled HR professionals can help contribute to more informed choices. This module is part of a qualification that is intended to provide a route to professional membership of the CIPD if you wish to develop a career in HR management. It will also provide training in research and academic skills if you want to develop an academic career in the field of HR management.

B870A.title: Managing in a changing world-Management
B870A.description: The module provides you with the opportunity to develop and learn about managing and marketing in relation to your working life and personal practice. As an aspiring organisational decision-maker, you'll gain the knowledge and tools necessary to successfully take advantage of cutting-edge theories of management and human resource management. This will be linked to the values of collective responsibility, aesthetics and ethics. You'll become empowered to create responsible growth, across a range of private sector, public and not for profit organisations, while also critically reflecting on your own potential in terms of leadership and management practice. In addition, you'll explores the ways in which marketing can be used to more effectively help organisations to be both successful and forward thinking in a business environment that is quickly moving beyond traditional geographic, cultural and organisational boundaries. The module offers a developmental route appropriate for the first module of an MBA, which builds on and consolidates knowledge through a series of activities and text.

B870B.title: Managing in a changing world-Marketing
B870B.description: B870 Part B Managing in a changing world. While studying this module, you will be encouraged to develop, as well as challenge, your current knowledge and skills in order to meet the contemporary and rapidly changing areas of management, marketing, ethics and leadership. Using both independent and collaborative approaches to learning, this module will enable you to integrate and understand ways of managing these core business functions in the face of globalisation, technological advancements and other recent economic, social and political challenges. B 870 B Theme provides a coherent and strong conceptual narrative to the module. These overarching themes provide a way of relating different and disparate knowledge to a conceptually organised framework. The theme consists of, Unitarism and Pluralism, challenges the idea that there is one best way and the assumption that when we speak of ‘an organisation’ we are talking about one harmonious and homogenous entity.

B872.title: Creating and sustaining value-Financial Management
B872.description: This course is an elective for the direct entrants to the Finance track of the MBA programme. The scope of this course relates to the central managerial aspects of understanding, creating, improving and sustaining value within contemporary organisations. This course will enable the participant to gain a greater understanding of how decisions and organisational performance can be optimised.
